LA VERNE YOUTH & FAMILY ACTION COMMITTEE
  Minutes of the Regular Meeting
  January 28, 2020

1. A regular meeting of the Youth & Family Action Committee was called to order by
  Mayor Don Kendrick at 6:30 p.m.

2. Executive Board Members present:

  Executive Board
  Don Kendrick, Chair
  Robin Carder, Council Member
  Matthew Lyons, BUSD
  Carolyn Cockrell, BUSD
  Denise Fisher, Resident

  Mark Rodgers, BUSD
  Krista Weismair Henrick, BUSD
  Michael Gaydos, Student Representative
  Joe Otto, Oak Mesa PTA
  Jason Lorge, Resident
  Ron Serven, Resident
  Isabella Alva, American Lung Association
  Jessica Vozella, American Lung Association
  Kim Luna, American Lung Association
  Karina Funez, American Lung Association
  Marissa Scholefield, David & Margaret
  Michael Miller, David & Margaret
  Sam Gonzalez, LVPD
  Hollie Savage, LVPD
  Francisco Cambero, LVPD
  David Yim, Tri-City
  Isela Moreno, Tri-City
  Irene Oseguera, Tri-City
  Bill Aguirre, City of La Verne
  JR Ranells, City of La Verne

3. Review of Minutes  Minutes for the November 26th meeting were
  approved.

4.  School Resource Officer  School Resource Officer (SRO) Frankie Cambero
  provided information on a possible tool to help
  address the ongoing use of vaping products by
  community youth. This relates to a citation process
  that is not currently being used. The group
  discussed educational options for first time offenders
  and progressing to stronger measures for additional
  infractions.
 Youth & Family Action Committee Minutes January 28, 2020, page 2

5. BUSD Report  Mark Rodgers with the BUSD provided a report on
  activities within the district. Mark provided
  information on a new pilot program for students
  caught with controlled substances. Mark also shared
  information on recent K-9 visits to schools and a
  successful grant application that will support career
  technical education.

6. School Counseling Program  David Yim with Tri-City Mental Health Services
  reported information from December referrals to the
  school counseling program. David also shared how
  Ekstrand Elementary was processing mental health
  services in a different way that might be something to
  model in other BUSD schools.

7. American Lung Association  Jessica Vozella and Isabella Alva with the American
  Lung Association provided a thorough presentation on
  addressing the youth vaping epidemic. Isabella is also
  a student at Bonita High School and provided her
  perspective of vaping issues. The group discussed
  strengthening the City’s retail tobacco license. Staff
  will work with Jessica on suggested amendments and
  bring back for further discussion and direction.

  Isabella is working on her senior project related to
  vaping issues and will come back to present the
  project at the April 28th YFAC meeting.

8. Round Table  Hollie Savage with the La Verne Police Department
  thanked the group for supporting the Public Safety
  Open House. Hollie noted that the department was
  still receiving inquiries into the “Drive Like You Live
  Here” signs.

  SRO Cambero shared information on technology
  advancements and equipment available to officers.
  SRO Cambero noted Lt. Gonzalez and his particular
  efforts in obtaining resources.

  Lt. Gonzalez noted efforts to stem tobacco and vape
  products to underage users and also shared an update
  on recruitment efforts for the next SRO.

  Krista Weismair Henrik with Ramona Middle School
  discussed the importance of taking the stigma out of
  mental health and anxiety.
 Youth & Family Action Committee Minutes January 28, 2020, page 3

  Joe Otto with the Oak Mesa PTA shared his
  background and his interest in being involved with the
  committee.

  BUSD School Board Member Matt Lyons shared that
  the State of the District will be presented on February
  25th at 11 a.m. Mr. Lyons also noted that the BUSD
  has broadened programs and focused on intervention
  for those less served. He also shared the district’s
  best days are ahead.

  Michael Miller with David & Margaret expressed his
  appreciation for La Verne’s ability to build effective
  relationships.

  Marissa Scholefield with David & Margaret shared
  information on programs and resources available as
  well as a new drop in center.

  David Yim with Tri-City Mental Health Services
  discussed the importance of building trust in order to
  provide better service and better support our youth.

  Isela Moreno with Tri-City Mental Health Services
  provided information on the upcoming stakeholders
  meeting, programs available through Tri-City’s, an
  upcoming hiring event at the Wellness Center and a
  grant available for groups interested in early
  intervention and wellbeing.

  Resident Ron Serven wanted the group to remember
  today’s date related to a wellness initiative in the early
  stages. Ron mentioned working with the
  La Verne/San Dimas Education Foundation on
  important programs to benefit the community.

  Denise Fisher provided an update on the K9
  Foundation and an upcoming fundraiser banquet that
  is in the early planning stages.

  Mark with the La Verne Bicycle Coalition promoted the
  benefits of Safe Routes to Schools and discussed with
  the group the importance and potential of partnerships
  that could be utilized for grant funding.

  JR Ranells with the City of La Verne updated the
  group on the new YFAC accounts through facebook,
  Instagram, and Twitter.
 Youth & Family Action Committee Minutes January 28, 2020, page 4

  Council Member Robin Carder thanked the group for
  their participation and shared information on the
  upcoming Health and Fitness Fair as well as the
  Community Yard Sale on April 18th at BHS.

  Bill Aguirre with the City shared information about the
  Open Streets event taking place April 19th.

9.  Public Comment  None

10.  Next Meeting  The next YFAC meeting is scheduled for February
  25th at 6:30 p.m.

11. Adjournment  The meeting was adjourned at 8:20 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

JR Ranells
Personnel Officer
